title: OLX Group: Regional Platforms, Verticalization and Retreat
basis: Reconstructed on 2026-11-12 from the published index.md (paragraph for paragraph, in its own order) and spec.md (accepted 2026-10-21), which it replaces. Intent outcome, the four acceptance criteria, the thesis and the role are copied unchanged from the case-olx entry in journal-spec.json. A roadmap paragraph (p04), an interpreting paragraph under the vertical table (p43) and a conclusion section (p57, p58; p58 is the published closing paragraph moved under its own heading) were added.

know: OLX's four dated phases: roll-up and rebrand (2006–2018), regional reshaping through mergers and joint ventures (2018–2021), the vertical integration bet with OLX Autos (2019–2025), and the retreat to a European core of seven markets (2022–2026: US$992 million revenue, a 48% adjusted EBITDA margin, 71% from motors, real estate and jobs).

The engineering record by era: search in five stages on one engine (sort, formula, learning to rank in Solr, a separate paid-visibility objective, hybrid retrieval), the hybrid-search proof sequence, one repository with per-brand configuration, and what the record leaves out (which brands share code, La Centrale's integration, the event backbone).
believe: A shared platform is worth the markets it serves for as long as the group keeps them.
Adjacent inventory and transactional businesses should be built to be retired cheaply, and a live search stack is improved in place with a proof sequence.
can_do: Ask, before funding a shared capability, which markets will still be in the group in five years.
Lay out a proof sequence for adding a new retrieval method to a live search stack, with a revenue guardrail.

audience.who: Chief and enterprise architects of marketplace groups, search and ranking leads, and engineering directors deciding which markets and adjacent businesses a shared platform should serve, and how to change a live search stack.
already_knows: What an API, a database, an event stream, a search engine and Kubernetes are, and the basics of machine learning.
Part IX's evidence rules (documented fact, the author's reading, labeled inference), from part-9 and case-adevinta.
Learning to rank, paid visibility in ranking and hybrid retrieval, from ranking and query-understanding; tenancy and consolidation, from multi-country-platforms and platform-consolidation.
Veldmark, its brands and its 2027-2028 decisions, from meet-veldmark and the chapters.
does_not_know: OLX Group's corporate history, brands and owners (Naspers, Prosus).
Prosus's profit measures aEBIT and aEBITDA and its fiscal year ending 31 March.
OLX-internal names: VAS LTR, Vanilla LTR, the extension chain, Pay&Ship, Otodim, AutoIQ.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Given a proposed inventory business and a planned search-engine replacement, the reader uses OLX's dated record to say how each should be built or changed.
acceptance_criteria.probe: A classifieds group wants to buy and resell used cars beside its listings, and its search team proposes replacing its Solr cluster to add vector search. Using only this chapter: what does OLX's record show for each, and how would you build or change them?
acceptance_criteria.expected: OLX Autos reached US$1.6 billion of revenue in the year to March 2022, just over half of the classifieds business, while losing money, and Prosus exited it from 2023; so keep money with a licensed provider, inventory systems outside the listing core, a separate data boundary and events, and per-category feature flags, so a retreat is a configuration change. OLX kept Solr and BM25 and added vectors as a fixed quota, retrained the ranker, shipped a modest ranker to collect data, and proved it in a smaller market's zero-results fallback before the main flow; vector retrieval at first penalized paid listings until the ranker was retrained, so add a revenue guardrail to every retrieval change.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader of the opening alone (the callouts and the paragraphs before the first heading) can predict the chapter's questions, its evidence and where it ends.
acceptance_criteria.probe: After reading only the callouts and the paragraphs before the first heading: what questions will this chapter ask, what kind of evidence will it use, and how will it end?
acceptance_criteria.expected: Three questions asked of each phase (which markets and businesses the platform carried, what the group bet on beyond listings, what the engineers published about the stack meanwhile); evidence from Prosus and OLX filings and an engineering blog spanning 2018 to 2026 that describes three different organizations and many markets OLX no longer owns; the arguments that liquidity and platform value are local, adjacent bets must be built to be retired, and a listing stack is improved in place; a final comparison with Veldmark.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reverse outline of the chapter, written without the spec, lists the same controlling ideas in the same order as the post spec's sections and paragraphs.

Every statement about OLX's internal systems that no cited source documents sits in a callout or figure caption labeled as inference, and every company fact outside those labels carries its source and publication year.
acceptance_criteria.probe: Is there any sentence outside an `INFERENCE, NOT DOCUMENTED` callout or a labeled figure caption that describes how OLX builds or runs a system without a dated source, or a company fact with no source and year?
acceptance_criteria.expected: None. Undocumented internals appear only in labeled inference callouts or captions; each company fact names its source and year in the sentence or the timeline; the author's interpretation is marked 'my reading' or sits in the Chief Architect's view.

thesis.question: What happened to OLX Group's listing platform as its portfolio shrank from 45 markets to seven and its adjacent businesses were exited, and what did its engineers change in the listing stack meanwhile?
thesis.claim: OLX's record shows that the portfolio, not the platform strategy, set what its shared platform was worth: every market it left between 2018 (45 markets) and its year to March 2026 (seven) took its stack with it, and its inventory and transactional bets, led by OLX Autos, were exited or de-prioritized; meanwhile the listing stack improved by evolution in place, with Solr and BM25 kept, ranking moved into the engine, paid visibility given its own objective and vector retrieval added as a fixed quota proved first in a smaller market's fallback path; so a group should fund shared capabilities for the markets it will keep, build adjacent businesses to be switched off, and change search through a proof sequence rather than a replacement.
thesis.disputed_by: The view that breadth across many markets is what makes a group's shared platform pay; that a classifieds group should move into owning inventory and handling transactions to capture more of each sale; and that adding vector search or modern ranking requires replacing the incumbent search engine.
thesis.so_what: A Chief Architect asks which markets will still be in the group in five years before funding a shared capability, and designs it so the others can leave; keeps an adjacent business's money with a licensed provider, its inventory systems outside the listing core and its entry points behind per-category flags; adopts OLX's hybrid-search proof sequence as a standard; makes paid visibility a named objective with an owner and puts a revenue guardrail next to the relevance metric of every ranking or retrieval change; and starts consolidation with identity and service-estate hygiene, measured in services migrated.
thesis.how_why: OLX rolled up and rebranded local sites across four continents, merged regional businesses into joint ventures, sold Avito in 2022 and left markets through sales, mergers and joint ventures. OLX Autos reached US$1.6 billion of revenue in the year to March 2022, just over half of the classifieds business, while losing money, and Prosus exited it from 2023; pay-and-ship was de-prioritized in Europe and the credit broker and services marketplace were sold. By the year to March 2026 OLX was seven markets with US$992 million of revenue, a 48% adjusted EBITDA margin and 71% of revenue from motors, real estate and jobs. Through all of it the engineering blog documents search moving from sort to formula to learning to rank in Solr, a separate 'VAS LTR' objective for paid visibility, and hybrid retrieval rolled out in a fixed sequence after it was found to penalize paid listings; multi-brand work moved to one front-end repository for three brands and one learning-to-rank repository with per-brand configuration.

supporting_claims.claim: The portfolio, not the platform strategy, set what OLX's shared platform was worth: between 2018 (45 markets) and its year to March 2026 (seven) every market that left through a sale, merger or joint venture took its stack with it, and the margin rose as the portfolio narrowed to motors, real estate and jobs.

OLX's inventory and transactional bets, led by OLX Autos (about half of classifieds revenue in the year to March 2022 while losing money), were exited or de-prioritized within about six years, so adjacent businesses should be built to be switched off.

Meanwhile the listing stack improved by evolution in place: Solr and BM25 kept, ranking moved into the engine as learning to rank, paid visibility given its own objective and measured causally, vector retrieval added as a fixed quota proved first in a smaller market's fallback path, and multi-brand work moved to one repository with per-brand configuration.

The record is dated and uneven: eight years of engineering posts describe three different organizations, documented fact, the author's reading and labeled inference stay apart, and the evidence stops at which brands share code, La Centrale's integration and the event backbone.

role.contribution: Shows the portfolio, not the platform strategy, changing what a shared platform is worth, adjacent bets retired, and a listing stack evolved in place while the group around it shrank.

additional_patterns.applies_to: trade-offs, verticals, failure-modes and evidence-stops: the record read across the phases
chief-architect to questions: from the author's rules to the book's patterns, Veldmark and the reader's own group

flow.rationale: The rules and the timeline come first because every later fact is read in their terms. The four phases follow in time order, because each phase changed what the platform had to carry and the reader needs the portfolio before the stack. The engineering record follows the phases because it describes the business that remains after them. The cross-cutting sections draw on both and must follow them; where the evidence stops comes before the author's rules so they are not read as documented; the comparison with the book and Veldmark and the questions to ask come last because they apply the rules. The phases overlap, and the timeline lead says so. Phase 2 (mergers, from 2018) comes before Phase 3 (the inventory bet, from 2019) although their dates overlap, because the mergers shrank the footprint first and the bet's story runs on to 2025, into the retreat. Trade-offs come before vertical differences and failure modes because they name the options the other two qualify; the comparison with the book and Veldmark precedes the questions because the questions turn its verdicts into checks on the reader's own group.

sections.heading: Phase 1: Roll-Up and Rebrand (2006–2018)

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Secondary sources agree that Naspers bought into OLX in 2010, raised its stake to about 95% in 2014 and that year rebranded acquired local leaders to OLX while vertical brands kept their names.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The posts of 2022 to 2026 describe OLX Europe, the business that remains, and concentrate on search, ranking, recommendations, experimentation, trust and safety and language models on the supply side.
OLX's search evolved through five stages on one engine, Apache Solr, the best-documented search evolution in the book's research.

evidence.what: Sort only; hand-tuned formula; LambdaMART in Solr's learning-to-rank plugin (+12% conversions on page one, +5% purchases, +4% unique buyers); 'Vanilla LTR' and 'VAS LTR'; hybrid retrieval with BM25 plus a fixed number of vectors.
evidence.shows: Each stage extended the engine already running.

transition_in.introduces: The first and best-documented one.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Learning to rank trains a model to order results from labeled outcomes, and NDCG is the standard offline ranking metric; both are defined in the ranking chapter.

transition_in.carries_over: The terms in the stage table.
transition_in.introduces: Their one-line glosses.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Two choices in OLX's ranker match the book's patterns: a contact as the success label, with a check that unique contacted sellers rose, and paid visibility as an explicit separate objective, the opposite of Multiplier Creep.

evidence.what: A classifieds platform rarely observes the sale; a ranker can concentrate demand on a few sellers; whoever changes the ranker must see the paid objective.
evidence.shows: Why each choice matters.

transition_in.introduces: What their design choices show.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The September 2025 hybrid-search post describes the order of proof as well as the design: a quota of vectors beside BM25, a ranker retrained to judge them, a modest ranker to collect data, and a first test in a smaller market's fallback path.

evidence.what: 'We began with 35 results from semantic search', later 'from 35 to 70'; the LTR model 'consistently assigned lower relevance scores to vector search results', a problem for VAS ads; 'a linear re-ranking model to temporarily replace LTR'; seller-contact events more than doubled in the fallback; about 3% on apps and about 5% on mobile web in the main flow.
evidence.shows: Each step limited what could go wrong.

evidence.what: Figure 4: the hybrid design as OLX described it in 2025.
evidence.shows: The documented shape, not internal components.

transition_in.carries_over: The last row of the stage table.
transition_in.introduces: How that step was proved.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Similarity is not relevance in local classifieds: a companion 2025 post shows a similar-items test losing until location and price were brought back through re-ranking.

evidence.what: October 2025 post on offline evaluation: model chosen by memory, latency and language; offline dataset weighting favorites and chat replies above clicks.
evidence.shows: Embeddings alone do not capture what makes a local listing relevant.

transition_in.introduces: A second limit on vector retrieval.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Beyond ranking paid listings, OLX treats its paid products (boost packages and VAS) as claims to be measured, using propensity matching against self-selection and group sequential testing against peeking.

evidence.what: Premium motors packages 'appeared to perform worse' because 'professional sellers self select'; matched uplifts of 17.6% to 97.4% (August 2026); with daily peeking 'despite a significance level of 5%, 27.9% of the simulations yielded a significant result' (August 2025).
evidence.shows: Paid visibility is measured causally, not from dashboards, and peeking is controlled because it inflates false positives more than fivefold.

transition_in.carries_over: Paid listings ranked by the ranker's separate paid objective.
transition_in.introduces: How the value of the paid products to sellers is measured.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The record has three explicit, recent statements about multi-brand engineering: one front-end repository for three brands, one learning-to-rank repository with brand configuration, and identity and service-estate clean-up across 71 services.

evidence.what: 'One-product, three brands' (February 2026); 'all LTR projects within a single repository' with Hydra configuration (June 2025); 'standardized user identification across 71 services, with 73% now using modern UUIDs' and 'too much of everything, not enough of anything' (March 2026).
evidence.shows: Cross-brand work ran on configuration over one code base and needed clean-up first.

transition_in.introduces: How the same stack serves several brands.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: An August 2026 post mentions a change across three codebases, two Go services and a PHP service, and a labeled inference reads the fragments as one code base per vertical serving several country brands by configuration.

evidence.what: 'three codebases': two Go services and a PHP service.
evidence.shows: Go and PHP services coexist.

evidence.what: Figure 5: a reference reading of OLX Europe's multi-brand shape; all but the brand names, the ranking repository and La Centrale is inference.
evidence.shows: Assembles the fragments, labeled.

evidence.what: INFERENCE, NOT DOCUMENTED callout: a plausible reference architecture; which brands share which code base is not published.
evidence.shows: Keeps the inference apart from the record.

transition_in.introduces: A fourth fragment that fits them, and what the fragments together suggest.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The rest of the record (moderation, duplicates and fraud rings, chat fraud, media and recommendations) belongs to the chapters that own each topic, and a table summarizes it with dates and links.

evidence.what: Five areas with what OLX published, date and era, and the owning chapter.
evidence.shows: The record's breadth, routed to the chapters that develop it.

transition_in.introduces: The remaining topics of the record.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: OLX's 2025-2026 releases describe generative AI mostly on the supply side and in new channels, with company-reported outcomes.

evidence.what: Posting time cut 35-55% (2025); Auto Description 98% style and relevance, 89% faithfulness (2026); job-role extraction at 'approximately 15K per month' for about 4,000 calls a day (2024); AutoIQ; CompassGPT and AutoGPT as apps inside ChatGPT (2026).
evidence.source: OLX Group releases and tech blog, 2024-2026
evidence.shows: Language models went first to listing creation and to channels OLX does not control.

transition_in.introduces: The newest part of the record.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: In my reading the ChatGPT apps are the architecturally significant item, because serving inventory to an assistant OLX does not control turns structured attributes, availability and API-grade access into the product.

transition_in.introduces: The one with the largest architectural consequence.

sections.heading: The Chief Architect's View
sections.controlling_idea: The record yields five decision rules, each conditioned on the evidence: let the portfolio decide what the platform is worth, price adjacent bets as closable, change search with a proof sequence, make paid visibility a named objective, and start consolidation with identity and service-estate hygiene.

advances_thesis.how: Turns the thesis into the author's labeled decision rules.

flow.rationale: The portfolio rule comes first because the others assume a known set of markets; the adjacent-bet rule follows because it decides what the platform carries; the three engineering rules close, from the search sequence the record documents best to the hygiene work that precedes consolidation.

transition_in.introduces: The author's decision rules drawn from it.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: What I take from OLX is a set of decision rules, each conditioned on the evidence.
Let the portfolio decide what the platform is worth: before funding a shared capability, ask which markets will still be in the group in five years and design it so the others can leave.

transition_in.introduces: The first rule.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Price adjacent bets as businesses that may be closed, keeping money with a licensed provider, inventory outside the listing core, a separate data boundary and events, and entry points flagged per category.

transition_in.introduces: The rule for adjacent businesses.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Change the search stack by evolution with OLX's hybrid-search proof sequence adopted as a standard.

evidence.what: Figure 6: a six-step staircase from keeping keyword search to the main flow.
evidence.shows: Each step limits what can go wrong.

transition_in.introduces: The rule for changing search.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Make paid visibility a named objective with an owner, and put a revenue guardrail next to the relevance metric of every ranking or retrieval change.

transition_in.introduces: The guardrail it needs for paid listings.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Treat identity and service-estate hygiene as the start of consolidation, scheduled first and measured in services migrated.

transition_in.introduces: The last rule, on consolidation.

conclusion.heading: From OLX to eBay Classifieds
conclusion.synthesis: Asked of every phase, the three questions give one answer: which markets the platform carried was decided by deals, not by the platform; what the group bet on beyond listings was exited or scaled back; and what the engineers published shows the stack that stayed improving in place one proved step at a time. In my reading these are one rule: a shared platform is worth the markets the group keeps, so adjacent businesses should be easy to switch off and search should change in steps that can be stopped.
conclusion.so_what: A Chief Architect cannot choose the portfolio but can choose a platform that follows it: funded for the markets that stay, with adjacent businesses that can be switched off and a search stack changed in stoppable steps.
